content: 1. Health centers are now able to receive stock information from community-level providers via text messaging. This system allows decision-makers at all levels to access previously unavailable community-level data, enhancing their ability to make informed decisions. 2. Feedback from users of this system has been overwhelmingly positive, and best practices are being developed to optimize its use. The program is being expanded to additional districts, with similar initiatives already operational in Ethiopia and Rwanda. 3. A baseline assessment conducted in 2010 aims to measure the program's impact on the availability of essential health products. This initiative is adapted from JSI's cStock program, which uses SMS technology to improve the supply of child health medicines for community case management (CCM) in Malawi. 4. In 2011, the World Health Partners (WHP) launched the Skymeds network in Bihar, India, under the Ananya initiative funded by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation. This program has significantly improved access to rapid, affordable, and high-quality treatments for infants close to their homes. 5. The success of the Skymeds program is attributed to the engagement of rural private providers, who are often the first point of contact for 70-80% of rural families seeking care for life-threatening conditions like pneumonia and diarrhea. These providers have been encouraged to adopt best practices for detecting and managing childhood illnesses. 6. Telemedicine has been employed to connect rural private providers with qualified doctors, thereby enhancing the quality of care. A robust supply chain ensures the availability and affordability of essential medicines, such as oral rehydration salts (ORS), zinc, and amoxicillin, for treating pneumonia and diarrhea. 7. To further combat childhood pneumonia in Bihar, innovative tools are being explored. These include Android-based respiratory rate timers to detect fast breathing (a key symptom of pneumonia), low-cost pulse oximeters for hypoxia detection, and oxygen concentrators or generators to address oxygen supply shortages in rural areas. 8. Generating demand for health services involves advocacy and communication strategies targeting political and community levels. Providing information, education, and communication to health workers, private sector providers, families, and the general public is essential for raising awareness and promoting care-seeking behaviors. 9. Key family and community practices that significantly impact child health have been identified. Interventions targeting these practices can substantially reduce child mortality and morbidity while improving child development outcomes. 10. Communication strategies must be evidence-based, consistent, and tailored to the target audience. Resources should be allocated to ensure effective communication, which includes monitoring and evaluation to measure impact. 11. The Global Coalition Against Child Pneumonia, through initiatives like World Pneumonia Day (WPD), has successfully raised awareness and mobilized resources to combat pneumonia. Advocacy efforts continue year-round to sustain momentum and engage stakeholders. 12. In Pakistan's Haripur district, the Lady Health Workers (LHW) program trained community health workers to manage severe pneumonia in children using oral amoxicillin. Advocacy and community engagement efforts increased care-seeking behavior, with 50% of pneumonia cases being treated by LHWs after two years of program implementation. 13. In Bangladesh, the Baby Zinc mass media campaign promoted the use of zinc and ORS to combat childhood diarrhea. The campaign utilized formative research to understand community beliefs and practices, employing multiple communication channels to ensure message clarity and acceptance. 14. The Baby Zinc campaign achieved high product awareness, with 95% in urban areas and 50% in rural areas, primarily through television. Promotional activities included courtyard meetings, folk songs, and a popular television drama series to sustain interest and encourage zinc use. 15. Communication strategies for child survival programs must be structured, research-driven, and linked to program goals. They should address the information needs of the target audience and include rigorous monitoring and evaluation. 16. Public-private partnerships have been instrumental in improving access to essential health commodities. For example, collaborations have reduced the cost of long-acting contraceptives and increased the availability of ORS and zinc for diarrhea treatment. 17. In Benin, working with wholesalers to market Orasel Zinc through commercial distribution channels increased its availability from 36% to 58% within a year. Training and engaging private providers further improved prescription practices. 18. Cleaner energy initiatives, such as Indonesia's conversion of over 40 million homes from kerosene to LPG for cooking, demonstrate the potential of public-private partnerships to address health and environmental challenges.
